question: Should OpenClaw keep repairing the released `skills/skill-creator/scripts/init_skill.py` helper, or treat it as obsolete now that current main directs durable skill creation through `skill_workshop`?
rationale: The shipped release contains the case-sensitive parser, but current main removed the helper and the open fix PR conflicts, so automation cannot safely choose between release compatibility and the newer skill-creation direction.

options.title: Treat the helper as obsolete
options.body: Close or redirect this issue and the linked PR because current main no longer exposes the helper and documents `skill_workshop` as the supported path.

options.title: Repair the released helper
options.body: Revive or backport case-insensitive parsing for `init_skill.py` with focused tests if maintainers still consider that helper a supported release surface.

recommendation.title: Treat the helper as obsolete
recommendation.body: Close or redirect this issue and the linked PR because current main no longer exposes the helper and documents `skill_workshop` as the supported path.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter appears on both the original skill-creator introduction and the current-main skill-creator shape, making him the best available owner for the supported-surface decision.
